testimony:
Action A1 (send generator to NICU)  
1 Maxim: “When one lifesaving device can aid either a small group facing certain, imminent death or a larger population facing less-certain, later harm, allocate it to the group in certain, imminent peril.” Universalizability: All rational agents could will this; the rule specifies a non-arbitrary, timing-based criterion and is self-consistent.  
2 Satisfies: rescue (imminent), non-instrumentalization, impartiality toward vulnerability.  
   Violates: imperfect rescue toward residents, possible justice worry about unequal benefit.  
3 Classification: PERMISSIBLE.  
4 Conflict: imperfect rescue duties to two groups. Priority rule: A perfect/immediate life-preservation duty overrides an imperfect, probabilistic one (Groundwork §II).  
5 Numerical magnitude: SECONDARY—figures mark scope but do not override the immediacy criterion.

Action A0 (send generator to water plant)  
1 Maxim: “When a single device can avert a large but probabilistic future harm, prefer that use even if a small group will certainly die immediately.” Universalizability: Rational agents facing immediate certain death could not will this, for they would be authorizing their own abandonment; the maxim fails the contradiction-in-will test.  
2 Satisfies: imperfect rescue for residents, public justice.  
   Violates: stringent rescue for eight infants (near-perfect), treats them as dispensable, strains impartiality.  
3 Classification: PROHIBITED.  
4 Conflict: same as above; immediacy-based perfect duty to the infants has priority over broader imperfect rescue.  
5 Numerical magnitude: SECONDARY.

frozen_baseline.reason: Declares A1 permissible and A0 prohibited because perfect, immediate rescue for infants overrides imperfect, probabilistic rescue for residents under universalizability and duty hierarchy.

framework_commitments.A0: PROHIBITED: Fails contradiction-in-will; abandons persons in certain, imminent peril, violating perfect rescue and treating them as dispensable.
framework_commitments.A1: PERMISSIBLE: Satisfies perfect duty of immediate life-preservation, respects non-instrumentalization and impartiality toward the most vulnerable.
